memory_update.text: Within this candidate chunk, direct chokepoint exposure ranks strongest for MU, SSNLF, 000660.KS, VRT, AVGO, and MRVL because they map to HBM/memory, data-center physical infrastructure, custom AI silicon, AI networking, and optical/data-movement nodes.

NVDA and AMD are core AI compute demand drivers and create pull-through for HBM, packaging, power, and cooling, but they should be treated as visible demand-driver nodes rather than under-discovered bottleneck candidates without a market-pricing check.

MTZ, ITRI, and NEE are derivative power-grid beneficiaries: the thesis depends on whether large-load data-center demand converts into signed utility capex, PPAs, interconnection upgrades, grid-edge contracts, or executable backlog.

MTZ requires project-level evidence tying Power Delivery or Clean Energy backlog to data-center interconnection, substation, or transmission work; current evidence shows backlog and segment exposure but not data-center-specific causality.

ITRI requires customer/order evidence proving that utilities are buying grid-edge intelligence or demand-response tools specifically because of large-load/data-center growth rather than general AMI and resiliency spending.

SMCI requires elevated verification because its relationship to the theme is operationally direct but vulnerable to margin compression, accounting quality, customer concentration, inventory risk, and platform-qualification risk.

For all HBM names, the next critical evidence is not just roadmap announcements but qualified volume shipments, customer allocation, yield, packaging capacity, pricing duration, and whether non-HBM DRAM tightness persists.

For AVGO and MRVL, the key diligence path is to separate AI networking, custom silicon, and optical/interconnect revenue from broader semiconductor or software revenue, then test customer concentration and duration of design wins.

summary: Layer 2B maps one candidate chunk of the New Hotspots funnel into public-market relationships across AI data-center power execution, grid-edge visibility, firm/clean power procurement, data-center power/cooling systems, AI server integration, accelerator/networking demand, and HBM/DRAM bottlenecks. Highest direct bottleneck mappings in this chunk are HBM/memory suppliers, data-center physical infrastructure suppliers, and AI networking/custom silicon; utility/EPC/grid-edge names are more derivative and require project-level evidence linking backlog or bookings to data-center large-load demand.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Check latest 10-Q/earnings-call transcript for explicit data-center, substation, transmission, utility large-load, or hyperscaler references; split backlog growth between Power Delivery and Clean Energy and test whether awards are regulated utility capex or generic infrastructure.
ticker_relationships.relationship: MasTec maps to the execution layer of power-delivery work: utility transmission and distribution, clean-energy infrastructure, substations, and related construction that may be pulled forward by large-load interconnections and grid expansion. The relationship is plausible but not yet proven to be data-center-specific from available evidence.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Verify whether Itron contracts, bookings, or segment commentary specifically reference data centers, large-load management, demand-response enrollment, power-quality monitoring, or AI-enabled distribution-grid analytics.
ticker_relationships.relationship: Itron maps to a second-order grid-access node: utility grid-edge intelligence, visibility, forecasting, power-quality management, and demand-response capabilities that become more valuable as electrification and data-center loads increase.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Track signed hyperscaler PPAs, data-center hub disclosures, interconnection status, generation project CODs, storage attachment rates, and whether data-center demand improves returns rather than just adding capex and regulatory risk.
ticker_relationships.relationship: NextEra maps to large-load power procurement through renewable energy, storage, gas, nuclear and utility-scale development capabilities. Its relationship is stronger if hyperscaler data-center campus demand converts into signed PPAs, generation additions, or transmission/storage projects.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Validate order growth, backlog, capacity additions, liquid-cooling mix, hyperscaler concentration, book-to-bill, lead times, pricing power, and margin sustainability in the most recent filings and call transcript.
ticker_relationships.relationship: Vertiv maps directly to AI data-center physical infrastructure, especially critical power, thermal management, liquid cooling, and rack-density enablement. This is a cleaner picks-and-shovels relationship than utility names because the company sells into the data-center buildout layer.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Check latest audited filings, cash conversion, customer concentration, gross-margin trajectory, DLC rack capacity utilization, NVIDIA/AMD platform qualification, inventory quality, and any auditor/regulatory/accounting updates.
ticker_relationships.relationship: Super Micro Computer maps to AI server and rack-scale integration, including direct-liquid-cooled systems for high-density GPU clusters. It is closer to system integration than to a unique component bottleneck, so evidence must separate volume growth from margin, customer, accounting, and competition risks.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Use market-pricing checks: revenue expectations, hyperscaler capex sensitivity, Blackwell/Rubin supply ramp, networking growth, HBM supply allocation, export-control exposure, and whether consensus already embeds peak-margin assumptions.
ticker_relationships.relationship: NVIDIA maps to the primary AI compute demand node and pulls through HBM, advanced packaging, networking, power, and cooling demand. It is a core demand driver but less differentiated as an under-discovered chokepoint because the relationship is highly visible and broadly priced by the market.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Verify AI accelerator revenue disclosures, named customer deployments, HBM4 supply agreements, MI350/MI450/MI455X ramp timing, ROCm adoption, gross margins, and whether demand is incremental or share-shifted.
ticker_relationships.relationship: AMD maps to AI accelerator and data-center CPU demand, with HBM pull-through through Instinct GPUs and future MI-series platforms. The relationship depends on customer traction, software ecosystem adoption, supply allocation, and competitive positioning versus NVIDIA and custom ASICs.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Track AI semiconductor revenue, networking versus custom-accelerator mix, number and quality of hyperscaler customers, design-win duration, supply-chain constraints, and whether VMware/software margins obscure semiconductor cyclicality.
ticker_relationships.relationship: Broadcom maps to custom AI accelerators and AI networking for hyperscalers, a non-GPU AI infrastructure node that can benefit from scale-out cluster growth, Ethernet switching, and custom silicon design wins.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Check AI bookings conversion, data-center revenue concentration, custom-silicon program ramps, optical DSP attach rates, customer concentration, gross margins, and whether demand is broad-based or concentrated in a few programs.
ticker_relationships.relationship: Marvell maps to AI data movement: optical DSPs, 800G/1.6T connectivity, Ethernet switching, custom XPU and XPU-attach solutions, and data-center interconnect. It is a second-order AI bottleneck candidate where cluster scale increases networking and optical intensity.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Verify HBM revenue, HBM generation mix, customer qualifications, 2026-2027 sold-out status, capex plans, DRAM pricing, non-HBM bit supply, and whether cycle pricing is already reflected in consensus.
ticker_relationships.relationship: Micron maps directly to the HBM and DRAM bottleneck. AI accelerator growth increases demand for HBM and can tighten conventional DRAM supply through capacity allocation, pricing, and advanced packaging constraints.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Confirm customer qualification status, commercial shipment volumes, HBM4 yields, HBM4E sampling progress, NVIDIA/AMD platform attachment, foundry base-die constraints, and whether HBM gains offset broader semiconductor cyclicality.
ticker_relationships.relationship: Samsung Electronics maps to global HBM/DRAM supply and advanced memory roadmap execution. HBM4/HBM4E progress can reshape AI memory supply availability and competitive share versus SK hynix and Micron.

ticker_relationships.next_evidence: Verify latest HBM share, NVIDIA/other customer qualification, HBM4 and 16-high roadmap, capex and wafer-capacity plans, advance purchase commitments, pricing duration, and downside if competitors close the qualification gap.
ticker_relationships.relationship: SK hynix maps to one of the most direct HBM bottleneck nodes, with strong relevance to AI accelerator supply chains, customer qualification, capacity allocation, and advanced DRAM supply tightness.
